basics.name: OpenSCAD libraries list (openscad.org Libraries page, with MCAD, NopSCADlib and the other notable mechanism/joint libraries)
basics.url: https://openscad.org/libraries.html (official list). Related lists: https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/OpenSCAD_User_Manual/Libraries (OpenSCAD User Manual page with the MCAD section and an older 'Other libraries' list) and https://github.com/openscad/openscad/wiki/Libraries (older GitHub wiki list, read via its raw source)
basics.resource_type: CAD library (a curated directory of OpenSCAD code libraries; each listed item is itself a CAD library)
basics.cost: Free (the list and every library on it)
basics.license: The list page states no licence for its own text (the footer is empty) [uncertain], so treat the page itself as all rights reserved but freely linkable. The Wikibooks version is CC BY-SA 4.0. Each library has its own licence, which the official page shows next to it: e.g. BOSL and BOSL2 BSD-2-Clause, NopSCADlib GPL-3.0-or-later, dotSCAD LGPL-3.0, UB.scad CC0, BOLTS LGPL-2.1/GPL-3.0, threads.scad CC0, STEMFIE parts GPL-3.0, Mark's Enclosure Helper GPL-3.0; MCAD is LGPL 2.1 (per its README)
basics.language: English (a few libraries have non-English names inside the code, e.g. UB.scad uses German module names such as Gewinde (thread), Glied (hinge) and CyclGetriebe (cycloidal gear))
basics.year: OpenSCAD's GitHub wiki libraries list and the Wikibooks list are older (the Wikibooks list still links Google Code and Google+ pages, so parts date from about 2013-2015); the Wikibooks page was last edited 26 March 2026. The openscad.org page is current: it lists StoneAgeLib, which needs 'a OpenSCAD version of at least 2025', so it was updated in 2025 or later [uncertain on exact date]. MCAD dates from about 2010 (involute_gears.scad is 'copyright 2010 GregFrost'). NopSCADlib's changelog runs to v21.43.1 on 24 September 2026
basics.access_barrier: none to read the list and the library docs; a desktop install of OpenSCAD is needed to generate parts (MCAD is bundled with OpenSCAD, the others must be downloaded)
basics.image_license: The official list has almost no images (a few example images are commented out in the page code). Library images (e.g. NopSCADlib's rendered part images, BOSL2's wiki renders) follow each library's own licence (GPL-3.0 for NopSCADlib, BSD-2 for BOSL2) [uncertain, not stated separately]
basics.authority_level: community or unvetted (the list is kept by the OpenSCAD project, which gives it some official standing, but the libraries are community projects of mixed quality; the Wikibooks page itself says MCAD bundles 'a lot of stuff, of varying quality')

coverage.covers: The official page lists 29 libraries in two groups. General (11): BOSL, BOSL2 (beta), dotSCAD, NopSCADlib, UB.scad, Functional OpenSCAD, Constructive, StoneAgeLib, BOLTS, Asset Collection, Board game toolkit. Single Topic (18): Round Anything, Mark's Enclosure Helper, funcutils, threads.scad, Smooth Primitives, Function Plotting, ClosePoints, Tray, YAPP project box generator, STEMFIE Parts Library, Catch'n'Hole, Pathbuilder, SCON, Altair's 2D Library, Doll house, Dimensions, LEGO.scad, Technic.scad. MCAD is NOT on the openscad.org page; it is described on the Wikibooks page as the library bundled with OpenSCAD. The libraries most relevant to connections and mechanisms are: BOSL2 (clips, snap pins, dovetails, hinges, Hirth joints, gears, threads - see its own entry); MCAD (involute and bevel gears, nuts and bolts, bearings, screws and augers, stepper and servo mounts, teardrop and polyholes, trochoids, gridbeam, LEGO compatibility); NopSCADlib (148 sections of parts: printed flat hinge, door hinge and door latch, press-fit connectors, drag chain, strap handle, knobs, printed pulleys, involute gears, plus 'vitamins' such as magnets, an OpenGrab electro-permanent magnet, circlips, springs, heat-set inserts, shaft couplings, rod ends, belts, pulleys, leadnuts, rails); UB.scad (thread, ball and roller bearing, hinge, double hinge, snap/clip-in pin, cycloidal gear, spring-loaded axle clamp); Mark's Enclosure Helper (hinged boxes with snap-fit catch clasps, magnet or screw closures, dovetails for joining boxes); STEMFIE (a printable construction toy of interlocking connections and fasteners); threads.scad; Catch'n'Hole (nut catches, screw holes); LEGO.scad and Technic.scad; Board game toolkit (boxes with catches). The older Wikibooks and GitHub-wiki lists add a U-Joint (universal joint) library, a roller-chain sprocket module, a '2D connection library' for joining laser-cut sheets, aluminium-extrusion connectors and a pinball parts library
coverage.organisation: A short flat page with two groups, 'General' and 'Single Topic', and a jump menu at the top. Each entry has a one-paragraph description, a Library link, a Documentation link and a licence. There is no search, no tags and no grouping by function, so you have to read the blurbs to know that, say, Mark's Enclosure Helper has snap-fit catches. It is easy to read but gives no route from 'I need two parts to click together' to a library
coverage.scope_match: low to medium. The list itself is a directory of code libraries, not a catalogue of connection types, and most entries are general geometry tools. A handful of the listed libraries (BOSL2, NopSCADlib, UB.scad, MCAD, Mark's Enclosure Helper, STEMFIE) do generate in-scope connection and mechanism types, and NopSCADlib's vitamins are largely standard hardware, which is out of scope
coverage.taxonomy_used: Two top-level groups only: 'General' (broad libraries) and 'Single Topic' (focused libraries). Inside the libraries: MCAD groups files as 'Currently provided tools', 'Tools (alpha and beta quality)', 'Very generally useful functions and constants', 'Other' and external utils; NopSCADlib groups its 148 sections into six columns: Vitamins A-H, Vitamins I-Q, Vitamins R-Z (bought-in parts), Printed (printed parts), Utilities and Core Utilities
coverage.example_types: Snap pin / clip-in pin (UB.scad Pin, BOSL2 snap_pin); Rabbit clip (BOSL2); Dovetail joint (BOSL2, Mark's Enclosure Helper); Print-in-place hinge (BOSL2); Living hinge (BOSL2); Flat hinge with filament pin (NopSCADlib flat_hinge); Double hinge (UB.scad DGlied); Snap-fit catch clasp (Mark's Enclosure Helper); Magnetic catch (Mark's Enclosure Helper, NopSCADlib magnets); Electro-permanent magnet (NopSCADlib OpenGrab EPM, magnetised and de-magnetised electronically); Press-fit connector (NopSCADlib press_fit, optionally glued or solvent-welded); Door latch (NopSCADlib); Retracting strap handle printed in flexible filament (NopSCADlib); Cable drag chain with 45 degree max bend per link (NopSCADlib); Cycloidal gear (UB.scad CyclGetriebe); Involute spur and bevel gears (MCAD involute_gears, NopSCADlib gears); Universal joint (U-Joint library, older list); Roller chain sprocket (older list); Hirth joint (BOSL2); Heat-set threaded insert (NopSCADlib inserts); Circlip / retaining ring (NopSCADlib); Rod end / spherical bearing (NopSCADlib); Shaft coupling (NopSCADlib); Swiss picture clip (NopSCADlib); LEGO Technic-compatible pins and beams (Technic.scad); Laser-cut sheet connections (2D connection library, older list)
coverage.making_methods: Mainly 3D printing (FDM) and parametric CAD; NopSCADlib also targets CNC-routed sheet parts (DXF) and 3D printer/electronics enclosure building; the older list includes laser-cut sheet joints and CNC drilling templates (pinball library)
coverage.item_count: 29 libraries on the openscad.org page (11 General, 18 Single Topic); about 25 more on the older Wikibooks 'Other libraries' list and about 20 on the old GitHub wiki list (with overlaps). Inside them: MCAD about 40 .scad files; NopSCADlib 148 documented sections; BOSL2 959 indexed functions and modules
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: torque-limiting: no library found; self-locking: not as a type (worm gears only in BOSL2); hand-release only: partly (BOSL2 locking rabbit clip with a release access point; snap-fit catch clasps in Mark's Enclosure Helper); one-way/ratchet: no dedicated ratchet module found; indexing/detent: partly (BOSL2 Hirth spline); over-centre: no; compliant: yes (BOSL2 living hinges and snap pins, UB.scad snap-in pin, NopSCADlib strap handle in flexible filament, snap-fit catches); print-in-place: yes (BOSL2 print-in-place hinge); gear trains/gearboxes: yes (MCAD involute and bevel gears, NopSCADlib involute gears and geared motors, UB.scad cycloidal gear, BOSL2 full gear set and planetary calculator); powered connectors: partly (NopSCADlib OpenGrab electro-permanent magnet, magnets, steppers, servos, geared motors, microswitches; no solenoid latch or motorised lock found); adhesive types: no (NopSCADlib press_fit only says 'add solvent or glue to make a permanent fixture')
coverage.entry_structure: On the list: name, one-paragraph description, Library link, Documentation link, licence. Inside NopSCADlib: part name, short description, links to the definition, implementation and test code, tables of properties, functions and modules, a rendered image, and a bill-of-materials style list of vitamins. Inside MCAD: only a bullet list of file names with a few words each
coverage.audience_level: hobbyist to professional (OpenSCAD users; NopSCADlib is aimed at people building 3D printers and electronics enclosures)

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: low. The list is short and readable, but it only tells you which code library to download; to get any connection you must install OpenSCAD and write code, and the libraries' docs are programming references. MCAD's docs are especially thin
usefulness.has_images: The official list: essentially none. The libraries: BOSL2 and NopSCADlib have many rendered images of every part (NopSCADlib has a full rendered catalogue in its readme and a gallery); MCAD has none in its README
usefulness.has_animations: no (none on the list or the MCAD/NopSCADlib readmes)
usefulness.gaps: No grouping by what the connection does; no search, tags or filters; no pictures on the list; MCAD (the bundled library) is missing from the official page and has minimal documentation; no torque-limiting, ratchet, detent, over-centre or cam-lock generators found in the listed libraries; no adhesive information; powered connectors only as off-the-shelf part models; mixed licences (GPL and LGPL libraries need care if code is reused); older lists contain dead links (Google Code, Google+)
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: partly. The list page has per-library anchors (e.g. https://openscad.org/libraries.html#NopSCADlib, #BOSL2, #STEMFIE), which are fine for a 'find more generators' link but not for single connection types. Individual parts are better linked in the libraries' own docs (e.g. BOSL2 wiki module anchors, or the #flat_hinge style anchors in NopSCADlib's readme on GitHub)
usefulness.reusable_data: The list is scrape-only (a small static HTML page, no API; no licence stated for the page), but the Wikibooks copy is CC BY-SA 4.0. The libraries themselves are in public Git repositories and are reusable under their own licences (BSD-2, MIT and CC0 ones freely; GPL/LGPL ones with conditions)
usefulness.maintained: Yes. The openscad.org page is current (lists libraries needing OpenSCAD 2025+). NopSCADlib is very active (release v21.43.1 on 24 September 2026). BOSL2 is active. MCAD looks largely dormant: its README says it is 'currently unfinished' and 'the maintainers aren't very responsive', and the Wikibooks page notes many unmaintained forks [uncertain on MCAD's last commit date]. The older GitHub-wiki and Wikibooks 'Other libraries' lists contain stale links
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) For each encyclopedia entry, a short 'Make it yourself' line naming a generator library and its licence, as the official list does (Library / Documentation / License). (2) NopSCADlib's split into 'vitamins' (things you buy) and 'printed' parts is a clear, beginner-friendly way to show whether a connection is printed, bought or both. (3) NopSCADlib's single-page catalogue with a rendered picture per part, and its rules written as plain notes (e.g. drag chain '45 degree maximum bend per link', flat hinge 'can bend back to 270 degrees'). (4) Grouping 'General' vs 'Single topic' is too coarse; the encyclopedia should group by function instead, which is the gap this list leaves
usefulness.design_rules_given: Not on the list. Inside libraries: NopSCADlib gives some (drag chain 45 degree max bend per link; flat hinge margins to open 270 degrees; gears profile-shifted below 19 teeth at 20 degree pressure angle, 7 teeth practical minimum; heat-set inserts pushed in with a soldering iron at 200 C); BOSL2 gives clearances for clips, pins and hinges (see its own entry); MCAD gives almost none (polyholes and teardrops are print-accuracy helpers)
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: yes, every listed library is a parametric OpenSCAD generator; the list itself is not
usefulness.file_formats: SCAD source for all libraries; OpenSCAD exports STL, 3MF, SVG and DXF. NopSCADlib's Python scripts also produce STL files for all printed parts, DXF files for CNC-routed parts, bills of materials and assembly manuals
usefulness.terminology_value: low for the list itself. Inside the libraries it is mixed: NopSCADlib uses standard supplier names for vitamins (circlips 'aka tapered retaining rings', rod ends 'sometimes called a spherical bearing or rod-end eye'), which helps with aliases; UB.scad gives German terms (Gewinde, Glied, Getriebe) useful for translations
usefulness.decision_support: none: no selector, filters or comparison tables, just two groups and short descriptions
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: The openscad.org page overlaps the older Wikibooks 'Libraries' page and the openscad GitHub wiki 'Libraries' page (both older and partly stale). BOSL2 has its own separate entry in this research, so do not double count it here. MCAD includes code taken from Thingiverse (involute_gears from thing:3575, teardrop from thing:3457); NopSCADlib's printed pulleys remix droftarts' Parametric Pulleys (Thingiverse thing:16627, CC BY-SA) and its gear maths follows KHK and tec-science references. BOLTS overlaps standard-parts catalogues (out of scope)
